schema.name: event-media
schema.title: Event Media
schema.description: A dwc:Event as content in an ac:Media entity.

fields.name: media_fk
fields.title: Media (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for an ac:Media resource.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the (Primary Key).
fields.rdfs:comment: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.

fields.name: event_fk
fields.title: Event (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the (Primary Key).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: subjectCategory
fields.title: Subject Category
fields.description: A term to describe the content of a image or a region of interest within an image using a controlled value string.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
fields.rdfs:comment: A term to describe the content of a image or a region of interest within an image using a controlled value string.

schema.name: event
schema.title: Event
schema.description: An action, process, or set of circumstances occurring at a dcterms:Location during a period of time.
schema.examples: `a material collecting event`; `a bird observation`; `a camera trap image capture`; `an organism occurrence`; `a biotic survey`
schema.rdfs:comment: An action, process, or set of circumstances occurring at a dcterms:Location during a period of time.

fields.name: event_pk
fields.title: Event (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: parentEvent_fk
fields.title: Parent Event (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a broader dwc:Event that contains this and potentially other dwc:Events.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the (Primary Key).
fields.examples: `A1` (parentEventID to identify the main Whittaker Plot in nested samples, each with its own eventID - `A1:1`, `A1:2`).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a broader dwc:Event that contains this and potentially other dwc:Events.

fields.name: eventCategory
fields.title: Event Category
fields.description: A broad category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a limited, tightly controlled vocabulary.
fields.rdfs:comment: A broad category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Event.

fields.name: datasetName
fields.title: Dataset Name
fields.description: A name of a source dataset.
fields.rdfs:comment: A name of a source dataset.

fields.name: eventConductedByID
fields.title: Event Conducted By
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of names of dcterms:Agents responsible for conducting or recording a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `José E. Crespo`; `Oliver P. Pearson | Anita K. Pearson`; `FMNH`
fields.rdfs:comment: A name for a dcterms:Agent responsible for recording a dwc:Occurrence.

fields.name: eventConductedByID
fields.title: Event Conducted By ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for conducting or recording a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY refer to a dcterms:Agent within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for recording a dwc:Occurrence.

fields.name: eventDate
fields.title: Event Date
fields.description: A date-time or time interval during which a dwc:Event occurred.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a date that conforms to ISO 8601-1:2019. Not suitable for a time in a geological context.
fields.examples: `1963-03-08T14:07-06:00` (8 Mar 1963 at or after 2:07pm and before 2:08pm in the time zone six hours earlier than UTC); `2009-02-20T08:40Z` (20 February 2009 at or after 8:40am and before 8:41 UTC); `2018-08-29T15:19` (29 August 2018 at or after 3:19pm and before 3:20pm local time); `1809-02-12` (within the day 12 February 1809); `1906-06` (in the month of June 1906); `1971` (in the year 1971); `2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z` (some time within the interval beginning 1 March 2007 at 1pm UTC and before 11 May 2008 at 3:30pm UTC); `1900/1909` (some time within the interval between the beginning of the year 1900 and before the year 1909); `2007-11-13/15` (some time in the interval between the beginning of 13 November 2007 and before 15 November 2007)
fields.rdfs:comment: A date-time or time interval during which a dwc:Event occurred.

fields.name: habitat
fields.title: Habitat
fields.description: A category or description of the habitat in which the dwc:Event occurred.
fields.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A category or description of the habitat in which the dwc:Event occurred.

fields.name: eventRemarks
fields.title: Event Remarks
fields.description: Comments or notes about the dwc:Event.
fields.examples: `After the recent rains the river is nearly at flood stage.`
fields.rdfs:comment: Comments or notes about the dwc:Event.

fields.name: locationID
fields.title: Location ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dcterms:Location.

fields.name: country
fields.title: Country
fields.description: The name of the country or major administrative unit in which the dcterms:Location occurs.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names. Recommended best practice is to leave this field blank if the dcterms:Location spans multiple entities at this administrative level or if the dcterms:Location might be in one or another of multiple possible entities at this level. Multiplicity and uncertainty of the geographic entity can be captured either in the term dwc:higherGeography or in the term dwc:locality, or both.
fields.rdfs:comment: The name of the country or major administrative unit in which the dcterms:Location occurs.

fields.name: countryCode
fields.title: Country Code
fields.description: The standard code for the country in which the dcterms:Location occurs.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use an ISO 3166-1-alpha-2 country code, or 'ZZ' (for an unknown location or a location unassignable to a single country code), or 'XZ' (for the high seas beyond national jurisdictions). Multiplicity and uncertainty of the geographic entity can be captured either in the term dwc:higherGeography or in the term dwc:locality, or both.
fields.rdfs:comment: The standard code for the country in which the dcterms:Location occurs.

fields.name: locality
fields.title: Locality
fields.description: The specific description of the place.
fields.comments: Less specific geographic information can be provided in other geographic terms (dwc:higherGeography, dwc:continent, dwc:country, dwc:stateProvince, dwc:county, dwc:municipality, dwc:waterBody, dwc:island, dwc:islandGroup). This term may contain information modified from the original to correct perceived errors or standardize the description.
fields.examples: `Bariloche, 25 km NNE via Ruta Nacional 40 (=Ruta 237)`; `Queets Rainforest, Olympic National Park`
fields.rdfs:comment: The specific description of the place.

fields.name: decimalLatitude
fields.title: Decimal Latitude
fields.description: A geographic latitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: Positive values are north of the Equator, negative values are south of it. Valid values lie between -90 and 90, inclusive.
fields.rdfs:comment: A geographic latitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of a dcterms:Location.

fields.name: decimalLongitude
fields.title: Decimal Longitude
fields.description: A geographic longitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: Positive values are east of the Greenwich Meridian, negative values are west of it. Valid values lie between -180 and 180, inclusive.
fields.rdfs:comment: A geographic longitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in dwc:geodeticDatum) of a dcterms:Location.

fields.name: coordinateUncertaintyInMeters
fields.title: Coordinate Uncertainty In Meters
fields.description: A horizontal distance (in meters) from a given dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude describing the smallest circle containing the whole of the dcterms:Location. Zero is not a valid value for this term.
fields.comments: Leave the value empty if the uncertainty is unknown, cannot be estimated, or is not applicable (because there are no coordinates).
fields.examples: `30` (reasonable lower limit on or after 2000-05-01 of a GPS reading under good conditions if the actual precision was not recorded at the time); `100` (reasonable lower limit before 2000-05-01 of a GPS reading under good conditions if the actual precision was not recorded at the time); `71` (uncertainty for a UTM coordinate having 100 meter precision and a known spatial reference system)
fields.rdfs:comment: A horizontal distance (in meters) from a given dwc:decimalLatitude and dwc:decimalLongitude describing the smallest circle containing the whole of the dcterms:Location. Zero is not a valid value for this term.

fields.name: footprintWKT
fields.title: Footprint WKT
fields.description: A Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the shape (footprint, geometry) that defines a dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: A dcterms:Location may have both a point-radius representation (see dwc:decimalLatitude) and a footprint representation, and they may differ from each other.
fields.examples: `POLYGON ((10 20, 11 20, 11 21, 10 21, 10 20))` (the one-degree bounding box with opposite corners at longitude=10, latitude=20 and longitude=11, latitude=21)
fields.rdfs:comment: A Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the shape (footprint, geometry) that defines a dcterms:Location.

fields.name: preferredSpatialRepresentation
fields.title: Preferred Spatial Representation
fields.description: An indication of which spatial representation best represents the dcterms:Location.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: An indication of which spatial representation best represents the dcterms:Location.

fields.name: informationWithheld
fields.title: Information Withheld
fields.description: Additional information that exists about a resource, but that is not shared publicly. Suggests that alternative data of higher quality may be available on request.
fields.comments: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `location information not given for endangered species`; `collector identities withheld | ask about tissue samples`
fields.rdfs:comment: Additional information that exists about a resource, but that is not shared publicly. Suggests that alternative data of higher quality may be available on request.

schema.name: identification
schema.title: Identification
schema.description: A classification of a resource according to a classification scheme.
schema.comments: For biology, the assignment of a scientific name or taxon concept to a dwc:Organism.
schema.examples: `a subspecies determination of an organism`; `a nomenclatural act designating a specimen as a holotype`
schema.rdfs:comment: A classification of a resource according to a classification scheme.

fields.name: identification_pk
fields.title: Identification (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for a dwc:Identification.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dwc:Identification.

fields.name: identificationType
fields.title: Identification Type
fields.description: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Identification.
fields.comments: The evidentiary basis, analytical approach, or inferential method by which an identification was determined. Values describe the dominant source of information supporting the identification (e.g., morphology, geography, molecular data, functional attributes, relationships, or taxonomic revision), independent of confidence level or taxonomic outcome.
fields.rdfs:comment: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Identification.

fields.name: materialEntity_fk
fields.title: Material Entity (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity based on which a dwc:Identification was made.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the (Primary Key).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.title: Scientific Name
fields.description: A scientific name string, not including authorship, date or identification qualifiers.
fields.comments: When applied to an Organism or Occurrence, this term should be used to represent the scientific name that was applied to the associated Organism in accordance with the Taxon to which it was or is currently identified. Names should be compliant to the most recent nomenclatural code. For example, names of hybrids for algae, fungi and plants should follow the rules of the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Shenzhen Code Articles H.1, H.2 and H.3). Thus, use the multiplication sign `×` (Unicode `U+00D7`, HTML `×`) to identify a hybrid, not `x` or `X`, if possible.
fields.examples: `Coleoptera` (order); `Vespertilionidae` (family); `Manis` (genus); `Ctenomys sociabilis` (genus + specificEpithet); `Ambystoma tigrinum diaboli` (genus + specificEpithet + infraspecificEpithet); `Quercus agrifolia var. oxyadenia` (genus + specificEpithet + taxonRank + infraspecificEpithet); `×Agropogon littoralis`; `Mentha ×smithiana`; `Agrostis stolonifera L. × Polypogon monspeliensis`
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name, with authorship and date information if known. When forming part of a dwc:Identification, this should be the name in lowest level taxonomic rank that can be determined.

fields.name: taxonRank
fields.title: Taxon Rank
fields.description: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the dwc:scientificName.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. The taxon ranks of algae, fungi and plants are defined in the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Shenzhen Code Articles H3.2, H4.4 and H.3.1).
fields.rdfs:comment: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the dwc:scientificName.

fields.name: kingdom
fields.title: Kingdom
fields.description: The full scientific name of the kingdom in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name of the kingdom in which the dwc:Taxon is classified.

schema.name: material-assertion
schema.title: Material Assertion
schema.description: A dwc:Assertion made by a dcterms:Agent about a dwc:MaterialEntity.
schema.rdfs:comment: A measurement of or fact about an rdfs:Resource (http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource).

fields.name: assertionID
fields.title: Assertion ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Assertion.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dwc:Assertion.

fields.name: materialEntity_fk
fields.title: Material Entity (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the (Primary Key).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: assertionType
fields.title: Assertion Type
fields.description: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Assertion.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:Assertion.

fields.name: assertionUnit
fields.title: Assertion Unit
fields.description: Unit associated with the value in dwc:assertionValue.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Ontology of Units of Measure http://www.wurvoc.org/vocabularies/om-1.8/ of SI units, derived units, or other non-SI units accepted for use within the SI. For units that are composed of multiple parts, use the patterns as given in "A Primer for Communicating Mathematics via Plain Text" (https://cse.sc.edu/~fenner/latex-ASCII.pdf) by Stephen Fenner (e.g., `g/cm^3` for grams per cubic centimeter). For other units, provide the value as a recognizable standard (e.g., '%') or written out in full and in the plural (e.g., `individuals`). It is fine to provide non-SI units in the original language of the dataset.
fields.rdfs:comment: A unit associated with the value in dwc:assertionValue.

schema.name: material
schema.title: Material
schema.description: An entity that can be identified, exist for some period of time, and consist in whole or in part of physical matter while it exists.
schema.comments: The term is defined at the most general level to admit descriptions of any subtype of material entity within the scope of Darwin Core. In particular, any kind of material sample, preserved specimen, fossil, or exemplar from living collections is intended to be subsumed under this term.
schema.examples: `the entire contents of a trawl`; `a subset of the contents of a trawl`; `the body of a fish`; `the stomach contents of a fish`; `a rock containing fossils`; `a fossil within a rock`; `an herbarium sheet with its attached plant specimen`; `a flower on a plant specimen`; `a pollen grain`; `a specific water sample`; `an isolated molecule of DNA`
schema.rdfs:comment: An entity that can be identified, exists for some period of time, and consists in whole or in part of physical matter while it exists.

fields.name: materialEntity_pk
fields.title: Material Entity (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: collectionEvent_fk
fields.title: Collection Event (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event during which a dwc:MaterialEntity was collected.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the (Primary Key).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: materialEntityType
fields.title: Material Entity Type
fields.description: A more generic classification of a dwc:MaterialEntity than dwc:preparations but less broad than dwc:materialCategory.
fields.comments: A more generic classification of a dwc:MaterialEntity than dwc:preparations. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `Macro-object`; `Micro-object`; `Oversized object`; `Cut/polished gemstone`; `Compound Specimen`; `Core`; `Mixed Materials`; `Environmental sample`; `Microscope slide`; `Spore print`; `Macrofossil`; `Mesofossil`; `Microfossil`; `Pinned object/specimen`; `Taxidermy mount`; `Blood sampling cards`; `Oversized fossil`; `Anthropogenic Artifact`
fields.rdfs:comment: A more generic classification of a dwc:MaterialEntity than dwc:preparations but less broad than dwc:materialCategory.

fields.name: institutionCode
fields.title: Institution Code
fields.description: A name (or acronym) in use by an institution having custody of a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.rdfs:comment: A name (or acronym) in use by an institution having custody of a resource.

fields.name: institutionID
fields.title: Institution ID
fields.description: An identifier for an organization.
fields.comments: For physical specimens, the recommended best practice is to use a globally unique and resolvable identifier from a collections registry such as the Research Organization Registry (ROR) or the Global Registry of Scientific Collections (https://scientific-collections.gbif.org/). The value in this field MAY refer to a dcterms:Agent within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for an organization.

fields.name: ownerInstitutionCode
fields.title: Owner Institution Code
fields.description: A name (or acronym) in use by an institution having ownership of a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.rdfs:comment: A name (or acronym) in use by an institution having ownership of a resource.

fields.name: ownerInstitutionID
fields.title: Owner Institution ID
fields.description: An identifier for an institution that owns a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: For physical specimens, the recommended best practice is to use a globally unique and resolvable identifier from a collections registry such as the Research Organization Registry (ROR) or the Global Registry of Scientific Collections (https://scientific-collections.gbif.org/). The value in this field MAY refer to a dcterms:Agent within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent.

fields.name: collectionCode
fields.title: Collection Code
fields.description: A name, acronym, coden, or initialism identifying a collection.
fields.rdfs:comment: A name, acronym, coden, or initialism identifying a collection.

fields.name: catalogNumber
fields.title: Catalog Number
fields.description: An identifier (preferably unique) for a dwc:MaterialEntity within a collection.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier (preferably unique) for a resource within a collection.

fields.name: preparations
fields.title: Preparations
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of preparations and preservation methods for a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of preparations and preservation methods for a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: disposition
fields.title: Disposition
fields.description: A current state of a dwc:MaterialEntity with respect to where it can be found.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A current state of a dwc:MaterialEntity with respect to where it can be found.

fields.name: derivedFromMaterialEntityID
fields.title: Derived From Material Entity ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:MaterialEntity from which this dwc:MaterialEntity was derived.
fields.comments: This dwc:MaterialEntity is separate from a dwc:MaterialEntity from which it was derived (cf. dwc:isPartOfMaterialEntityID). Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier. The value in this field MAY refer to a dwc:MaterialEntity within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a particular instance of a dwc:MaterialEntity.

schema.name: media
schema.title: Media
schema.description: A digital or physical media resource.
schema.comments: An instance of digital textual media may be better represented as a dcterms:BibliographicResource.
schema.rdfs:comment: A digital or physical media resource.

fields.name: media_pk
fields.title: Media (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for an ac:Media resource.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.
fields.rdfs:comment: An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.

fields.name: mediaType
fields.title: Media Type
fields.description: A category that best matches the nature of an ac:Media resource.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.
fields.rdfs:comment: The nature or genre of the resource.

fields.name: accessURI
fields.title: Access URI
fields.description: A URI that uniquely identifies a service that provides a representation of the underlying resource.
fields.comments: If this resource can be acquired by an http request, its http URL SHOULD be given. If not, but it has some URI in another URI scheme, that MAY be given here. Value might point to something offline, such as a published CD, etc. For example, the doi of a published CD would be a suitable value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A URI that uniquely identifies a service that provides a representation of the underlying resource.

fields.name: format
fields.title: Format
fields.description: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource, denoted by a controlled value string.
fields.comments: A controlled value string describing the technical format of the resource (file format or physical medium). The string SHOULD be a controlled value from the Audiovisual Core Controlled Vocabulary for Dublin Core dcterms:format, although it MAY be any Media Type (MIME type) value from the IANA list of Media Types (https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml) or any commonly used file extension string. Human-readable information about the Controlled Vocabulary for format is at http://rs.tdwg.org/ac/doc/format/. This term can be used to describe offline digital content. In cases where the provided Service Access Point URL includes a standard file extension from which the format can be inferred, it is permissible to not provide a value for this property. See also the entry for dcterms:format in the Audiovisual Core term list document and see the DCMI FAQ on DC and DCTERMS Namespaces, https://web.archive.org/web/20171126043657/https://github.com/dcmi/repository/blob/master/mediawiki_wiki/FAQ/DC_and_DCTERMS_Namespaces.md, for discussion of the rationale for terms in two namespaces. It is best practice to use dcterms:format instead of dc:format whenever practical. Normal practice is to use the same Label if both are provided. Labels have no effect on information discovery and are only suggestions.
fields.rdfs:comment: The file format, physical medium, or dimensions of the resource.

schema.name: molecular-protocol
schema.title: Molecular Protocol
schema.description: A protocol used to perform a dwc:NucleotideAnalysis and potentially derive a dwc:NucleotideSequence from a dwc:MaterialEntity.
schema.examples: `a standard DNA barcoding workflow using Sanger sequencing`; `a shotgun metagenomics pipeline for microbial community profiling`; `a high-throughput amplicon sequencing protocol targeting 16S rRNA`
schema.rdfs:comment: A protocol used to derive and identify a nucleotide sequence from a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: molecularProtocol_pk
fields.title: Molecular Protocol (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for a dwc:MolecularProtocol.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dwc:MolecularProtocol.

fields.name: assayType
fields.title: Assay Type
fields.description: A type of method used in a study to detect taxon/taxa of interest in a dwc:MaterialEntity.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
fields.rdfs:comment: A type of method used in a study to detect taxon/taxa of interest in a dwc:MaterialEntity.

fields.name: lib_layout
fields.title: lib_layout
fields.description: Specify whether to expect single, paired, or other configuration of reads.
fields.rdfs:comment: Specify whether to expect single, paired, or other configuration of reads.

fields.name: target_gene
fields.title: target_gene
fields.description: Targeted gene or locus name for marker gene studies.
fields.rdfs:comment: Targeted gene or locus name for marker gene studies.

fields.name: seq_meth
fields.title: seq_meth
fields.description: Sequencing method used; e.g., Sanger, ABI-solid.
fields.rdfs:comment: Sequencing method used; e.g. Sanger, ABI-solid.

fields.name: sop
fields.title: sop
fields.description: Standard operating procedures used in assembly and/or annotation of genomes, metagenomes or environmental sequences.
fields.rdfs:comment: Standard operating procedures used in assembly and/or annotation of genomes, metagenomes or environmental sequences.

fields.name: pcr_primer_forward
fields.title: pcr_primer_forward
fields.description: Forward PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. If multiple multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction, there should be a full row for each of these linked to the same dwc:Occurrence. The primer sequence should be reported in uppercase letters.
fields.rdfs:comment: Forward PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. If multiple multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction, there should be a full row for each of these linked to the same dwc:Occurrence. The primer sequence should be reported in uppercase letters.

fields.name: pcr_primer_reverse
fields.title: pcr_primer_reverse
fields.description: Reverse PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. If multiple multiple forward or reverse primers are present in a single PCR reaction, there should be a full row for each of these linked to the same dwc:Occurrence. The primer sequence should be reported in uppercase letters.
fields.rdfs:comment: Reverse PCR primer that were used to amplify the sequence of the targeted gene, locus or subfragment. schema.name: occurrence

fields.name: organismQuantity
fields.title: Organism Quantity
fields.description: A number or enumeration value for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.
fields.comments: A dwc:organismQuantity must have a corresponding dwc:organismQuantityType.
fields.examples: `27` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType); `12.5` (organismQuantity) with `% biomass` (organismQuantityType); `r` (organismQuantity) with `Braun-Blanquet Scale` (organismQuantityType); `many` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType)
fields.rdfs:comment: A number or enumeration value for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.

fields.name: organismQuantityType
fields.title: Organism Quantity Type
fields.description: The type of quantification system used for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.
fields.comments: A dwc:organismQuantityType must have a corresponding dwc:organismQuantity. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `27` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType); `12.5` (organismQuantity) with `% biomass` (organismQuantityType); `r` (organismQuantity) with `Braun-Blanquet Scale` (organismQuantityType); `many` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType)
fields.rdfs:comment: The type of quantification system used for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.

fields.name: lifeStage
fields.title: Life Stage
fields.description: An age class or life stage of a dwc:Organism.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: An age class or life stage of a dwc:Organism.

fields.name: vitality
fields.title: Vitality
fields.description: An indication of whether a dwc:Organism was alive or dead at the time of collection or observation.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: An indication of whether a dwc:Organism was alive or dead at the time of collection or observation.

fields.name: occurrenceStatus
fields.title: Occurrence Status
fields.description: A statement about the detection or non-detection of a dwc:Organism during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: For dwc:Occurrences, the default vocabulary is recommended to consist of 'detected' and 'notDetected', but can be extended by implementers with good justification. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.rdfs:comment: A statement about the detection or non-detection of a dwc:Organism during a dwc:Event.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.title: Scientific Name
fields.description: A scientific name string, not including authorship, date or identification qualifiers.
fields.examples: `Coleoptera` (order); `Vespertilionidae` (family); `Manis` (genus); `Ctenomys sociabilis` (genus + specificEpithet); `Ambystoma tigrinum diaboli` (genus + specificEpithet + infraspecificEpithet); `Quercus agrifolia var. oxyadenia` (genus + specificEpithet + taxonRank + infraspecificEpithet); `×Agropogon littoralis`; `Mentha ×smithiana`; `Agrostis stolonifera L. × Polypogon monspeliensis`
fields.rdfs:comment: The full scientific name, with authorship and date information if known. When forming part of a dwc:Identification, this should be the name in lowest level taxonomic rank that can be determined.

fields.name: taxonRank
fields.title: Taxon Rank
fields.description: A taxonomic rank of the most specific name in a dwc:scientificName.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. The taxon ranks of algae, fungi and plants are defined in the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Shenzhen Code Articles H3.2, H4.4 and H.3.1).
fields.rdfs:comment: The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the dwc:scientificName.

schema.name: survey
schema.title: Survey
schema.comments: This class includes properties found in the Humboldt Extension to Darwin Core (eco: namespace), except for the target scope terms, which can be accommodated in eco:SurveyTarget.
schema.examples: `a botanical survey of a protected area to assess native and invasive plant species`; `a wetland vegetation mapping`; `a camera trap deployment in a rainforest to monitor large mammals`; `a frog call survey in wetlands across breeding seasons`; `a coverboard survey for reptiles in forested environments`; `a pollinator survey in an agricultural landscape`; `a macroinvertebrate sampling in a freshwater stream to assess water quality`; `a habitat- or ecosystem-level survey (e.g., coral reef health assessment, forest biodiversity assessment)`; `an environmental impact assessment (e.g., pre-construction biological baseline survey for a wind farm project)`

fields.name: survey_pk
fields.title: Survey (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for an eco:Survey.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for an eco:Survey.

fields.name: event_fk
fields.title: Event (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the (Primary Key).
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for the set of information associated with a dwc:Event (something that occurs at a place and time). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.

fields.name: verbatimSiteNames
fields.title: Verbatim Site Names
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of original site names.
fields.comments: Site refers to the location at which observations are made or samples/measurements are taken. The site can be at any level of hierarchy. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `East Coastal Fringe | St. Marks Wildlife Management Area`; `S1 | S2 | C1 | C2 | R14 | R22 | W1`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list (concatenated and separated) of original site names.

fields.name: reportedWeather
fields.title: Reported Weather
fields.description: A list of weather or climatic conditions present during a dwc:Event.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a key:value encoding schema for a data interchange format such as JSON.
fields.examples: `flooding during week 3 of surveys`; `rockslide at site 2`
fields.rdfs:comment: A list of weather or climatic conditions present during the dwc:Event.

fields.name: verbatimTargetScope
fields.title: Verbatim Target Scope
fields.description: A verbatim original description of a dwc:Event scope.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is first to populate explicit scope terms to the fullest extent possible (e.g., eco:targetTaxonomicScope). It is not recommended to use this term in assessing absence or completeness.
fields.rdfs:comment: The verbatim original description of the dwc:Event scope.

fields.name: samplingPerformedByID
fields.title: Sampling Performed By
fields.description: A dcterms:Agent responsible for sampling.
fields.comments: The sampling dwc:Event could be at any level of hierarchy. In the case of a higher level (parent) dwc:Event, include all the organizations or people involved in the child dwc:Events that contributed to the parent dwc:Event. Recommended best practice is to separate multiple values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `North American Butterfly Association`; `KK Wall`; `JJ Green`; `LL Pink and FF Grey | Aspen Center for Environmental Studies`
fields.rdfs:comment: A person, group, or organization responsible for recording the dwc:Event.

fields.name: samplingPerformedByID
fields.title: Sampling Performed By ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for sampling.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to provide a single identifier that disambiguates the details of the sampling dcterms:Agent. If a list is used, the order of the identifiers on the list should not be assumed to convey any semantics. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `). The value in this field MAY refer to a dcterms:Agent within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.
fields.rdfs:comment: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent.

fields.name: isSamplingEffortReported
fields.title: Is Sampling Effort Reported
fields.description: The sampling effort associated with a dwc:Event was reported.
fields.comments: Typically values of effort would be captured under the terms eco:samplingEffortValue and eco:samplingEffortUnit. Recommended best practice is to follow the TDWG Boolean Controlled Vocabulary http://rs.tdwg.org/tag/doc/boolean/.
fields.rdfs:comment: The sampling effort associated with the dwc:Event was reported.

fields.description: A category that best matches the nature of a scope in an eco:SurveyTarget.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: surveyTargetValue
fields.title: Survey Target Value
fields.description: A value to include or exclude in a scope categorized by eco:surveyTargetType.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
fields.rdfs:comment: A value to include or exclude in a scope categorized by eco:surveyTargetType.

fields.name: includeOrExclude
fields.title: Include Or Exclude
fields.description: Whether to include or exclude eco:surveyTargetValue in a scope categorized by eco:surveyTargetType.
fields.comments: Combinations of eco:SurveyTarget records of inclusions and exclusions can define complex scopes such as all flying adult Aves except Passeriformes. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary consisting of 'include' and 'exclude' only.

schema.name: survey-target
schema.title: Survey Target
schema.description: One or more scopes that describe a target for dwc:Occurrences in an eco:Survey.
schema.examples: `all bird species`; `all bird species except Larus gulls, fulmars and kittiwakes`; `reproductive female Ctenomys sociabilis (only)`; `Oncorhynchus mykiss and Oncorhynchus clarkii (only)`, `all total lengths except < 12 inches`
schema.rdfs:comment: A specification of characteristics of dwc:Occurrences that were included or excluded in an eco:Survey.

fields.name: surveyTargetDescription

fields.name: isSurveyTargetFullyReported
fields.title: Is Survey Target Fully Reported
fields.description: Whether an eco:SurveyTarget can be used to infer absence of detection because all counts of detected dwc:Occurrences matching an eco:SurveyTarget were fully reported.
fields.comments: Recommended best practice is to follow the TDWG Boolean Controlled Vocabulary http://rs.tdwg.org/tag/doc/boolean/. If true (the survey target is fully reported - nothing was left unreported), then this enables inference of absence of detection for everything in that eco:SurveyTarget that is included but that does not appear in the counts (absent counts signify absence of detection).
fields.rdfs:comment: Whether an eco:SurveyTarget can be used to infer absence of detection because all counts of detected dwc:Occurrences matching an eco:SurveyTarget were fully reported.
